---
title: "About"
---

I was born in Bakersfield, California, a city famous for oil production, agriculture, and growing an astonishing number of carrots. Part of my childhood was spent in a town of fewer than 200 people in the Sequoia National Forest.

My path through higher education began at Bakersfield College, where I earned an A.S. in mathematics, followed by a B.S. at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo and a Ph.D. at UC San Diego. I've been fortunate to experience all three of California's public higher education systems as a student, and I'm grateful to the state for making these educational opportunities available.

Since then, my work has taken me to the University of Toronto Mississauga, Ghent University in Belgium, Umeå University in Sweden, Oregon Institute of Technology, and now [Cal Poly Humboldt](https://www.humboldt.edu), where I teach mathematics, statistics, and data science.

Along the way, I've worked on statistical methods and applications in medical research, developed an interest in causal inference and machine learning, and spent a great deal of time designing courses and projects. I enjoy figuring out how to approach a problem, choosing methods that make sense for the question, and making complicated ideas easier to understand and use.

Outside of work, I enjoy reading, walking, playing the violin, and making and eating cookies.
